This is a **finding** in the frozen driver (`dcitl_port.py`).

### Cause
- In [dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L319-L335), `Driver.step` handles unverified callers (`self.pid is None`) by parsing/extracting identity and calling `verify_identity`. Whenever no usable identifier is found or verification fails (`not res.get("ok")`), it unconditionally replies with `"I couldn't verify your identity, so I can't access appointments. Could you confirm your full name and date of birth (or member id)?"`.
- Unlike the workflow handlers (`route`, `book`, `cancel`, `reschedule`), which call [Driver.unclear](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L297-L306) to queue a human hand-off after 2 failed attempts, `Driver.step` has no retry counter, hand-off, or clean close for repeated identity failures.
- Meanwhile, in [truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L264-L272) and [policy.py](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L173-L191), `identity` sessions are designed with un-verifiable credentials (`no_credentials`, `first_name_only`, `wrong_dob`, `unknown_member`, `other_name_no_dob`) that `PatientPolicy.identity_parts` deterministically returns whenever asked for `"identity"`. Because `Driver.step` keeps re-asking indefinitely, every `identity` session loops until `PatientPolicy.patience` hits 0 and the patient gives up.

This is a **`finding`** in the frozen reference driver ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py)).

In `identity` scenarios ([truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/clinicbench/truth.py#L264-L272)), the patient is intentionally configured with unverifiable credentials (`no_credentials`, `first_name_only`, `wrong_dob`, `unknown_member`, or `other_name_no_dob`) and an empty `acceptable` set, expecting the clinic to either hand off or cleanly close ([contract-changes.md](file:///work/docs/contract-changes.md#L63-L65)). Accordingly, [`PatientPolicy.identity_parts`](file:///work/clinicbench/clinicbench/policy.py#L173-L191) repeats the patient's configured (failed) identifiers when re-asked.

However, in [`Driver.step`](file:///work/clinicbench/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L319-L335), when `self.pid is None` and identity extraction or `verify_identity` fails, the driver never increments a retry counter, never calls `self.unclear(...)` to escalate to `human_queue`, and never closes the conversation. Instead, it unconditionally re-asks `"I couldn't verify your identity, so I can't access appointments. Could you confirm your full name and date of birth (or member id)?"` on every turn until `PatientPolicy.patience` reaches 0 and the patient gives up.

This is a **finding** in the frozen driver ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py)):

1. In [truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L264-L272), `identity` sessions are constructed with an unverifiable `identity["mode"]` (`no_credentials`, `first_name_only`, `wrong_dob`, `unknown_member`, or `other_name_no_dob`), an empty `acceptable` set, and `handoff_ok = True`. By design ([policy.py](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L173-L191), [contract-changes.md](file:///work/docs/contract-changes.md#L63-L65)), [PatientPolicy.identity_parts](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L173-L191) deterministically returns that same unverified credential whenever asked for `identity`, expecting the clinician to either close cleanly or hand off after repeated failures.
2. In [Driver.step](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L319-L335), when `self.pid is None` and `ident` is empty or `verify_identity` returns `ok: False`, the driver unconditionally returns `"I couldn't verify your identity, so I can't access appointments. Could you confirm your full name and date of birth (or member id)?"` without incrementing `self.unclear_counts`, calling `self.unclear(...)`, handing off, or closing.
3. Because `Driver.step` loops on that prompt every turn, `PatientPolicy.patience` eventually reaches 0 and the session always ends in `give_up` (`gave_up`).
